subject: MAP: evaluation milestones, pilot credits and conversion economics

Subject: MAP: evaluation milestones, pilot credits and conversion economics

Hi Dana —

Following our demo last week, I put together a concise mutual action plan (attached) that lays out a 6-week evaluation and the milestone gates we discussed:

- Week 2: integration and baseline latency checks
- Week 4: quality validation on the priority prompt set
- Week 6: acceptance and production readiness review

Proposed commercial support for the evaluation: 150k free-generation-token credit (applied to the hosted API) plus one 1-week trial extension for the acceptance window. Credits are contingent on hitting the Week 4 quality gate and signing the MAP/SOW.

If Acme accepts the MAP and converts to a 12-month committed plan within 30 days of acceptance, we can offer a 20% first-year usage discount (applies to unit token price) and a 10% ramp credit carryover on month-1 overage. If the conversion is later than 30 days, the conversion discount steps to 10%.

I included a draft SOW and an acceptance test checklist for your engineering team to review. Can we lock in a short alignment call tomorrow to go over acceptance criteria?

Thanks —

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

Ben —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A couple of questions from our side before we commit to the MAP:

1) Can the 150k token credit be applied toward the Dedicated plan if we decide on an early conversion to committed capacity?
2) We need clarity on the acceptance criteria pass/fail definitions — specifically around performance percentiles (p95 latency) and quality thresholds for our top-10 intents.
3) Procurement will want the conversion discount written into the SOW; can you hold the 20% for signatures and provide a firm cancellation window?

We’re available for a 30-minute call Tuesday 10am ET. Aaron from product will join to walk through the quality targets.

Best,
Dana
VP Product | Acme Analytics

Dana —

Quick answers inline:
1) Credit portability: we typically apply pilot credits to the hosted account used during evaluation. For Dedicated conversions we can offer a one-time credit reconciliation: if you convert and commit within 30 days of acceptance we will apply up to 75% of remaining pilot credits as a one-time invoice credit toward the first month of Dedicated reserved capacity. I'll have finance confirm the exact accounting, but this is standard for conversion incentives.

2) Acceptance criteria: draft in acceptance_tests.xlsx — highlights: p95 latency < 450ms on your baseline workload (50-token median session), top-10 intent F1 >= 0.82 averaged across the test set, and false-positive rate for intent classification < 4%. These are pass/fail with an allowed single re-run window following remediation.

3) Discount language: we can put the 20% first-year usage discount into the SOW as conditional on execution of a 12-month committed agreement within 30 days of acceptance. Cancellation/exit: 30-day notice post-conversion; early termination fees apply per the SOW. If you need the discount guaranteed earlier we can discuss a signed term sheet first.

I've updated the MAP doc to add the credit portability clause and acceptance thresholds. Rishi, can you confirm the Dedicated reconciliation mechanics and whether we need any additional SKU mappings?

Call accepted for Tue 10am ET — invite sent.

Ben

Hi all —

Confirming the reconciliation approach: when Acme converts to Dedicated within 30 days of acceptance we will:
- Apply up to 75% of unconsumed evaluation credits against month-1 invoice for Reserved capacity (not toward one-time infra fees).
- Provide a one-time technical credit for a migration support workshop (up to 8 hours of SE time) to help move workload and validate KV cache behavior.

SKU mapping note: Dedicated has a base token unit price separate from hosted; reconciliation is an invoice credit (not a per-token rate match). We can include a sample invoice line in the SOW appendix.

I'll join Tuesday's call to walk through test harness and sample load profiles.

Rishi

Dana —

Appreciate the thoughtful questions and the productive call earlier today. Per internal approval: Redwood can commit to the following commercial terms if Acme signs the attached MAP + SOW within 14 days of acceptance testing pass:

- Evaluation support: 150k token credit (hosted) + 1-week trial extension
- Conversion incentive: 20% off first-year usage if 12-month commit is signed within 30 days of acceptance; 10% if signed between 31–60 days
- Credit reconciliation: up to 75% remaining pilot credits applied as invoice credit to month-1 Dedicated invoice upon conversion within 30 days
- Ramp protection: 10% month-1 overage credit applied back as credit if usage exceeds committed baseline

We also agree to a single quarterly review during the first three months post-conversion to ensure performance and cost alignment. Please find the final MAP/SOW attached and the DocuSign link below. We can finalize signatures and then schedule migration workshops.
